confirmed.statement: The counts are people, not drawings or ratings. Each participant drew one picture, and the two coders' scores were averaged into one score per drawing. From Table II's means and SDs, a pooled t-test with n = 58 and 55 gives t = 6.18, 10.34, and 9.31 (printed 6.20, 10.33, and 9.27). With the coders' ratings as units (116 and 110), t would be 8.73, 14.62, and 13.17.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds on S1 alone: 113 people analyzed, with 58 and 55 in the two arms.

Outside the people lens: Table I puts all eight 18-year-olds in the control group (0 of 58 against 8 of 55). Under individual random assignment, this split has probability about 0.002 (Fisher exact test). The paper also says the two groups were tested separately. These facts bear on criterion 1, not on the counts.
confirmed.quote: The group using generative AI and the group not using it were tested separately.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 663), Table I; PDF p. 2 (printed p. 662), Section II.A

summary: The form's people coding is right and each part has support in the text: 113 students were recruited and randomly assigned, Table I (after assignment) and Table II (every analysis) give 58 in the Kimi.AI arm and 55 in the no-AI arm with no exclusions, and the printed t statistics reproduce only with these person counts, so criterion 2 holds on this single study. Outside the people lens, Table I puts all eight 18-year-olds in the control group (probability about 0.002 under individual randomization) and the arms were tested separately, which the assignment check should weigh.
